why: THE DYNAMIC CONFIGURATION'S FLIP WHITELIST: the backend symbols the boundary may still carry when
--require-zero runs against build-release-dyn-clang64 (the runtime in root runtime/). ONE
CONFIGURATION, ONE PAIR (S5); this file and its baseline are the only boundary record left.
THE LIST IS DOWN TO THE DESIGNED BOUNDARY ITSELF, which is what the migration was for: after abi 18
the C entry is ONE symbol, and `deren_destroy_api_core` (deleted with the pointer-plus-deleter shape)
and `deren_abi_version` (folded into the call's first argument) are recorded under `departures`.
SET ONCE, FROM THE DYNAMIC TREE'S OWN MEASUREMENT, and only ever SHRUNK since: --update may only
shrink it, an entry with no live hit is a failure, an entry the ratchet never tracked is refused
(a new dependency cannot be whitelisted into existence), and --update never writes this file.

departures.left_in: ③-D/E step 2 (the merged runtime slice, abi 17)
departures.reason: initializer for module deren.vulkan.core. It was in this list as the one exception the import graph FORCED: the dynamic engine imported the backend module through two engine facades (vulkan/readback/readback.cppm and the legacy runtime's own declarations, the second of which this tree does not compile). The slice converted vulkan/readback to `rhi::api_core&` and dropped its import, so the initializer left the dynamic tree's measured set - the legacy runtime's file is the only importer left, and this tree does not build it. An exit, not a silence.

the deleter entry point is DELETED, not silenced: `deren_make_api_core` now RETURNS a `std::shared_ptr<api_core>` whose control block carries the backend's own deleter, so no host resolves a destroy symbol any more and the engine references none. The old spelling existed to keep "one C++ runtime" out of the boundary's premises; that premise is now measured and machine-checked (`cxx deren.exe imports libc++.dll`, which covers the backend DLL too), so the entry set went from three symbols to one. An exit, not a silence.

recorded for completeness rather than as a removed HIT: this symbol was never in the whitelist, because the engine never referenced it - it was an EXPORT the host called by name. It is deleted with the same batch: the version is now the entry's FIRST ARGUMENT, and a mismatch is refused with the backend's own number inside `error_info.native_code`. The export surface therefore carries exactly one `deren_*` symbol, which the DLL export gate checks on the artifact.

entries.reason: this is the DESIGNED boundary, declared in promise/rhi/backend_entry.hpp. The dynamic runtime is its only engine-side caller: it builds a shared_ptr<rhi::api_core> around deren_make_api_core(rhi::abi_version, &options, &error) and takes the face as *core_owner. It is what the design predicts the boundary to be, not a regression - and it never leaves while the backend is a DLL.
